new_statements.quote: The phonological word in Khmu consists of one, two or three syllables. The stress occurs on the main final syllable of the word. The majority of words are monosyllabic or disyllabic (sesquisyllabic). The presyllable C(C)V(C) of disyllabic words is unstressed and the vowel is just a transitional or reduced vowel. Examples from an EK dialect is provided.
new_statements.citation: Premsrirat, Suwilai. 2004. Register complex and tonogenesis in Khmu dialects. Mon-Khmer Studies 34: 1-17.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (page image of Premsrirat 2004, MKS 34, p. 10) and the scanned text lines 406-411. Under the heading '2) Syllables and word structure of Khmu' the page reads exactly: 'The phonological word in Khmu consists of one, two or three syllables. The stress occurs on the main final syllable of the word. The majority of words are monosyllabic or disyllabic (sesquisyllabic). The presyllable C(C)ᵛ(C) of disyllabic words is unstressed and the vowel is just a transitional or reduced vowel. Examples from an EK dialect is provided.' (only difference from the report: the presyllable vowel is printed as a superscript V). The examples (h'm'ma:l 'soul', tᶜla:m'pa:m 'butterfly' etc., stress mark…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Khmu words (1-3 syllables, mostly mono- or sesquisyllabic) carry a single stress on the final (main) syllable; presyllables are unstressed with a reduced/transitional vowel, and in the tonal Western Khmu varieties (incl. ct = Om Kae, Sipsongpanna) the presyllable is often deleted altogether. This is a statement about Khmu generally (seven dialects, two of them in Sipsongpanna, China), applied to kuan1250 only under Glottolog's hypothesis that 'Kuanhua' is Khmu spoken in Jinghong.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned; presyllables described as unstressed (no secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress placement. Trisyllables C(C)V(C).CV(C).'C(C)V(C) also final-stressed (examples tᶜlaːm'paːm 'butterfly', kᶜldɔŋ'dɛːŋ 'firefly'). WK tonal dialects ct/lb delete the presyllable, yielding monosyllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word, citation forms; statement is pan-dialectal for Khmu (EK and WK), with data from fieldwork 1996-2002 incl. two villages in Sipsongpanna (Yunnan). NOT a description of 'Kuanhua' by name — see identity_note.
new_statements.identity_note: kuan1250 'Kuanhua' is a Glottolog bookkeeping (retired) languoid with zero descriptive references; ISO xnh is still active. Ethnologue (E17, source EDCL 1991) itself says the speakers in Jinghong are 'locally considered part of Khmu peoples', and Glottolog (after Svantesson p.c. 2011) reads Kuan < kwɛɛn (Khmu Khuen/Kween ethnonym, cf. khue1238) and Damai < tmɔɔi 'subgroup', i.e. probably just Khmu [kjg, khmu1256] on the Chinese side; Wikipedia reports Li Yunbing 2005 instead classing 宽语 as 'Mangic' (unverified, print only). The quoted statement is Premsrirat's pan-dialect description of Khmu (khmu1256), whose sample includes two Sipsongpanna villages (Pung Soa = Eastern Khmu, Om Kae = tonal Western Khmu) but no variety named Kuan/Khuen in Jinghong. Khmu khmu1256 is already in CATALOG_V42 (StressTyp2, final stress, verified-clean), so cataloguing kuan1250 separately on this evidence would double-count one entity; hence candidate_for_catalog = false.
